newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power led lower by mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power led lower by mild weather.

text.p: Western U.S. spot power prices continued to sag amid above-normal temperatures throughout the region, but the trend could change next week if more seasonal weather returns, traders said.
"There is super mild weather throughout the West right now--we have no load," said one market source.

The Pacific Northwest will see temperatures 5 to 10 degrees F above normal through Saturday, but is expected to cool to slightly above-normal temperatures early next week, according to Weather Services Corp.
The Southwest is forecast to see above-normal temperatures through the weekend, but a snowstorm could develop over the Great Basin and Colorado Rockies by mid-week.
Traders noted that abundant hydroelectric supplies have also put a damper on prices.

The Northwest River Forecast Center this week raised its January-July runoff forecast at The Dalles dam on the Columbia River in Oregon to 137 percent of average levels, a rate which would exceed 1996's actual total of 132 percent of average.
Sources reported talk of curtailments at thermal power plants resulting from the ample hydropower supplies, but no cutbacks were confirmed.
Most coal-fired plants "have so many different participants it takes an act of god to do anything except maintenance," noted one trader.
He and others also said utilities are unlikely to risk turning off power plants at this time of year when weather patterns can change quickly.
Monday firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) was quoted at $9.50-10.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $11.00-12.00 for Friday.
Off-peak COB was little changed at $5.00-6.00.
Firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was down at $8.00-10.00, while off-peak was at $4.50-5.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was lower at $11.50-12.50, while off-peak was quoted at $6.00-8.00 per MWh.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $11.00-12.00, while off-peak was at $6.00-7.00.
